item.title: Kenny Beecham calls Warriors broadcast ‘the worst in the whole league’ after it defends Draymond Green
item.description: Credit: NBC Sports Bay Area The 2026-27 NBA season is underway, and while every NBA season brings plenty of change, it seems that some things are destined to always stay the same. The Golden State Warriors’ local NBC Sports broadcast team of Bob Fitzgerald and Kelenna Azubuike has finished in last place in Awful Announcing’s local NBA announcer rankings for three years running. Graders not only found Fitzgerald “condescending” and too focused on “teaching” the audience or complaining about referees, but the booth was also called out for its “homerism,” which even Warriors fans found excessive. That homerism reared its head again during Monday’s game between the Warriors and Phoenix Suns. Warriors forward Draymond Green was assessed a technical foul for throwing Suns center Khaman Maluach to the ground and escalating things with Suns guard Dillon Brooks afterward. However, if you let Fitzgerald and Azubuike tell it, everything Green did was within the lines. A notion so ridiculous that it wasn’t wasted on NBA content creator Kenny Beecham, who found himself on Awful Announcing’s 2026 list of rising stars in sports media. “I’m listening to this Warriors broadcast, and listen, they’ve been around for so long, this is not a new take, but I just remembered why the f*ck I don’t listen to the Warriors broadcast,” Beecham said on the Numbers On The Board podcast. Kenny speaks on the Warriors’ Broadcasters https://t.co/sWUceaucYB — Numbers On The Board (@notbpod) November 5, 2026 “It is the worst broadcast in the whole league by a wide margin, because every broadcast has to be biased. That’s why you listen to [Chicago Bulls announcer Adam Amin] and rest in peace, Stacey King. You want them to be Bulls fans, but also you don’t want them to be jack*sses while being Bulls fans. “And I feel like what they be doing in that Warriors broadcast is so jack*ssery where nobody can be wrong on the Warriors. Draymond grabbed Maluach, body-slammed him, and then choked Dillon Brooks! And it was like, ‘Well, I don’t know if they gonna get him on the choke.’ “Bro, Dillon Brooks face was purple!” Beecham and Awful Announcing’s readers are hardly alone in their assessment of Fitzgerald and Azubuike. Last year, Zach Lowe asserted that there was “no more homer broadcast in the entire NBA, and for all I know in the world of sports, than the Warriors’ broadcast.” We’re just barely past the 10% mark into the season, but it sounds like the Warriors broadcast is well on its way to its fourth consecutive last-place local announcer rankings finish. item.title: Packers Insider Gives Team Clear Directive Before Trade Deadline
item.description: The Green Bay Packers and general manager Brian Gutekunst have been heavily involved in the NFL rumor mill leading up to the November 10 trade deadline. No one knows whether or not the team will make a big move, but the rumors have been out there that they have shown interest. Most notably, the Packers have been heavily connected to a potential blockbuster trade for Indianapolis Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor. They aren’t viewed as the front-runner to make that move, but they have at least had interest in swinging big. Over the years, Green Bay has not been known as an aggressive buyer at trade deadlines. Instead, the Packers have focused on drafting and developing, while adding veteran pieces around the edges. The trade Micah Parsons last year helped change some of that lack of aggressiveness. So far this season, the team has looked like a potential contender in some moments and a team who could miss the playoffs in others. They have the talent to be a Super Bowl caliber team. However, a move or two is needed. With that being said, one longtime Green Bay insider has spoken out with a clear directive for the team before the deadline. Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) takes off on a run Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, during the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Green Bay Packers Urged to Get Aggressive at NFL Trade Deadline Sports Illustrated’s Bill Huber believes that it’s time for the Packers to make a Super Bowl move. He thinks they should be open to making a blockbuster trade. “To do big things requires bold actions. The Packers’ championship drought is too long. Now is the time to stop ‘being in every conversation’ and actually make the move to perhaps bring another title to Titletown,” Huber wrote . That statement from Huber is music to the ears of the fans. Green Bay has typically opted to not make the final move that could lead to a Super Bowl winning run. Making the trade for Taylor could be the final missing piece. The Packers could also consider an aggressive move to fix the offensive line like trading with the Philadelphia Eagles for Landon Dickerson. Only time will tell what Green Bay chooses to do. But, it’s clear that Huber and much of the Packers’ fan base believes that the time is now for Gutekunst and the front office to take a home run swing. item.title: ‘Social media made y’all way too comfortable’: Sophie Cunningham shares a message after election
item.description: Aug 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) looks on during the second half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Sophie Cunningham had plenty to say on social media the day after the midterm elections. After sharing a post about “being better Americans” on Wednesday, the Indiana Fever guard followed it up with another message. This time, Cunningham shared a blunt quote from boxing legend Mike Tyson to her Instagram story, which took aim at people who feel comfortable disrespecting others online. Cunningham’s Post-Election Message On Wednesday, a day after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, Cunningham reposted a lengthy message from podcaster and entrepreneur Andy Frisella to her Instagram story. The post argued that the country’s problems can’t be fixed through elections alone. “One of the strangest things about our culture is how much faith we’ve placed in elections to change our lives and how little faith we’ve placed in our own ability to do the same,” the post read. “Politics is downstream of culture. We can keep changing the people in charge, passing new laws and arguing over which party has the answers … but until we change the culture fostering, producing and tolerating the problems we have as a society, nothing fundamentally changes,” it continued. The post didn’t mention a party or candidate. But the timing was notable, coming from a player who has become a lightning rod for her political views. Cunningham sparked a firestorm this summer when she said she wants to protect girls from having to compete against “biological men,” comments that critics called transphobic. Still, Cunningham has insisted that her political views fall right in the middle . “I’m very much in the middle. I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides,” Cunningham told ESPN’s Hallie Grossman in July. Mike Tyson Quote Later, Cunningham shared another message to her Instagram story, this time a quote from Tyson. “Social media made y’all way too comfortable with disrespecting people and not getting punched in the face for it,” the post read, according to OutKick . Cunningham did not add any comment of her own, and it’s unclear what, if anything, prompted her to share it. She has been vocal about how she’s treated online, though. Earlier this week, Cunningham called her critics “ psychotic ” and said they have “so much hatred in their heart.” She also recently revealed that she has hired 24/7 security . item.title: Beach volleyball pro Alex Ukkelberg comes out: 'Thankful that I'm gay'
item.description: Alex Ukkelberg said he has been living his best life as an out gay man in Los Angeles for years, having come out to family, friends and in the pro beach volleyball community. But beyond that, it wasn’t until Wednesday that he said anything about it publicly. "There's no way I could be gay," the 32-year-old from tiny Battle Lake, Minnesota said in his coming out video . "Is there?" "When you grow up in a town of less than 800 people, being different is almost always a bad thing — and it’s definitely something you want to hide," Ukkelberg wrote in the caption. "I knew I was different from a young age.. but I didn’t know what that meant." “I’ve been out for a long time to family and friends and as I shared more on social media it just felt like a good thing to say. Visibility matters,” Ukkelberg told the LGBTQ+ sports site Outsports in an interview following his social media post. See on Instagram In his video, the former women's volleyball coach for the St. Cloud State Huskies talked about the various sports he played growing up: He ran track and competed in basketball, baseball, and football. Ukkelberg said while he knew he wanted to be an athlete, he said he thought that meant "there's no way I could be gay." That's the message he said the world reinforced, as he showed a flurry of images of him as both a student-athlete and as a guy dating women. Ukkelberg confessed that he actually didn't even think of himself as gay for many years. "Up until my sophomore year of college, I genuinely thought I was straight," he said, adding that he intensely felt the weight of finally admitting his identity for the first time. “Saying the words ‘I’m gay’ out loud for the first time was really hard for me,” said Ukkelberg. He added that he struggled with his sexuality so much that for a long time, he contemplated staying in the closet. But the toll of hiding who he was while pursuing sports was too much, he said. “After quite a few years of very bad mental health, I decided I wasn’t able to give up either identity. I was just going to have to figure out how to be both, and honestly, I’m thankful that I’m gay. It’s made me a better, more empathetic person,” said Ukkelberg. "I think I’ve always found it easier to let people get to know me first before I come out to them, rather than having to break through stereotypes just to be seen for who I am," he wrote in the caption to the video. "I’ve gotten it from both directions — too gay, not gay enough.. Nobody wants to be put in a box — especially not the young gay kid from a small town in rural Minnesota." item.title: Panthers sign ex-Eagles, Raiders cornerback before Week 9 game vs. Broncos
item.description: Panthers sign ex-Eagles, Raiders cornerback before Week 9 game vs. Broncos originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Carolina Panthers are sitting atop the NFC South heading into Week 9, but there is some real concern about this team with a 3-4 record following two brutal losses. They lost 43-13 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and then 27-19 to the Green Bay Packers . While their run defense struggled against the Buccaneers, their pass defense couldn't stop the Packers in Week 8. To try to fix things on the back end of the defense, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Panthers are signing 26-year-old cornerback Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad. Panthers sign Jakorian Bennett to bolster CB depth "The Panthers signed former Raiders and Eagles CB Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad," Rapoport reported. This isn't a massive move for the Panthers, but considering the team's shaky defensive back depth, Bennett might get real playing time in the not-too-distant future. Will Lee III, Mike Jackson, Akayleb Evans, and Jaycee Horn are all hurt right now. Only Lee has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Broncos . If Lee can't go, the Panthers will be down to relying on Malcolm DeWalt IV a lot, as the rest of their CB depth chart is banged up. Bennett might see a role right away as the Panthers' CB room is dealing with a lot of injury issues. item.title: Bo Naylor Reveals He Didn't Know Depths of MLB Gambling
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers catcher Bo Naylor If any MLB players didn't believe that allegedly fixing games came with serious consequences, the images from the federal trial involving Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz this week should have changed their minds. Clase and Ortiz were in New York on Thursday to face conspiracy charges for allegedly fixing individual pitches for prop bets during the 2025 season. Catcher Bo Naylor, who was a teammate of both pitchers with the Cleveland Guardians at the time, testified that he "didn't know" individual pitches could even be bet on. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "I didn't know that before," Naylor said, according to The Associated Press. "I didn't know that until (this) situation." Prosecutors expressed disbelief that Naylor could be unaware of the nature of such bets, according to the AP report, and showed video of multiple pitches that have been called into question. Naylor was called upon to testify because, as a catcher, he would have been involved in game-planning and calling pitches for Clase and Ortiz, and might have known if they didn't throw the pitches he'd called. When pitches missed the strike zone -- in some cases, spiked into the dirt or airmailed to the backstop -- Naylor testified that he simply chalked it up to even the best pitchers often missing their spots. Naylor appeared in 207 games as a catcher over the 2024-2025 seasons with Cleveland. He was limited to 27 total games with the Guardians this season before he was traded to the Milwaukee Brewers, with whom he played only three games. But Murray might not be the only starter missing on offense for the Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. In total, nine Vikings landed on Thursday’s injury report , and seven of them were limited in practice. Minnesota Vikings left tackle Christian Darrisaw dealing with a shoulder injury The most concerning one might be on the far left side of the offensive line. item.description: Official: Paul Nebel extends contract with Mainz 05 As officially announced by the Bundesliga club this afternoon, Paul Nebel has extended his contract with 1. FSV Mainz 05. The midfielder, who joined the club at Bruchweg as a 13-year-old, progressed through all the youth teams at Mainz's academy. item.title: Bijan Robinson Chases Acting Dreams Beyond The Field
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images While the Atlanta Falcons are fighting for their season, the 24-year-old running back is actively planning his life after the gridiron. He told the New York Post that he is taking serious steps to launch an acting career. He even wants to star in a romantic comedy. This is more than a hobby for a rich athlete. He is enrolling in acting classes to learn the craft from the ground up. He appeared as himself on the Disney Channel show “Bunk’d: Learning The Ropes” last July. He also made a cameo in the Netflix series “Outerbanks” in October. Those roles were fun, but he wants more. He said he is ready to move past commercials and into serious drama. “I’m willing to kind of explore anything more on the drama side,” Robinson said on behalf of Invisalign. A Plan for Life After Football The 2026 season has been tough for the Falcons. They sit at 3-5 after a 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Robinson knows the team needs him to be better. He has 780 rushing yards and four touchdowns so far. Yet he refuses to accept praise as the league’s top back. “I’ll be honest, like, I don’t feel like I’m playing like that right now,” Robinson said, in comments shared by Falcons reporter Daniel Flick. He demands more from himself for the offense to succeed. He launched his own DJ series called “Spin Zone” in September 2024. He sees these projects as a way to grow as a person. “I want to continue to put myself in different brackets of life,” Robinson said. He plans to dig deep into acting classes at the end of the year. He wants to gain the talent and charisma needed to succeed on screen, not just because he is an NFL star. Advice for Struggling Stars Robinson uses his own experiences to help others facing pressure. He is in Madrid this week to play the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 8. He plans to meet with Real Madrid soccer stars Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé before the game. Vinícius is going through a slump and dealing with a four-game suspension. Robinson offered simple advice to help the Brazilian player. “I’ll tell (Vinícius), just stay the course. Don’t worry about external noise,” Robinson said. He warned that listening to critics can hurt a player’s mind. He knows what it feels like to have bad weeks. He told Vinícius to trust that God’s plan for his career would be amazing. “If you have an up-and-down or a low or something like that, we all have those moments and we all had those weeks,” Robinson said. item.title: Oscar Piastri pays tribute to Australian F1 legend Alan Jones following his death
item.description: Motorsport photo McLaren's Oscar Piastri has paid tribute to Alan Jones following the death of Australia's 1980 Formula 1 world champion. Jones died at the age of 80 on 5 November 2026, following a short illness. He won 12 grands prix, celebrated 24 podium finishes and gave Williams its first drivers' title. He also remains the last Australian to have won the Australian Grand Prix at Calder Park in 1980. Jones competed in the championship from 1975 to 1981, in 1983 and again from 1985 to 1986. In addition to Williams, he also drove for Hesketh, Hill, Surtees, Shadow, Arrows and Haas-Lola. Speaking to F1.com at Interlagos ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix weekend, Piastri said: "It's obviously a very sad day. A life that should be very well celebrated. I think [he was] a guy who obviously had a lot of success on the racetrack and was Australia’s most recent world champion. "But I think also the person he was, you know, a very straightforward person, straight to the point. On a personal level as well, he often had nice things to say about me, which was nice." Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones The Australian driver revealed he had driven the Williams in which Jones won his title. "I’ve had the honour to drive his world championship-winning car as well, so [it was] very cool to be able to experience that and connect with him in some kind of way. A sad day, but a day that should celebrate a great life. "Obviously, he was a long, long time before me, and I never had much interaction with Alan. But I think in a lot of ways, he kind of embodied the Australian spirit – very tough, saying it how it is, saying what he thinks, and I think that’s probably the biggest thing. "Anyone who’s won a world championship in F1 has clearly achieved it through talent, hard work, all kinds of other things, so I think that probably says enough." item.title: RI’s Tyler Kolek takes a shot at Taylor Swift’s Knicks fandom
item.description: Taylor Swift was there at the New York Knicks' magical Game 4 to see the 29-point comeback last spring and the OG Anunoby tip-in , and while there were a lot of questions about whether or not she's a Knicks fan , she is. But when Knicks guard Tyler Kolek was asked who the "fakest" celebrity fan was for an NBA 2K League video on Thursday, Nov. 5, he threw out Swift's name, and his teammate Miles McBride agreed. "I don't know if I've seen her at any other games," Kolek said. But then he backtracked a bit. "I guess she's got a lot going on, so she can't come all the time," he added. "It's a little performative." As he and McBride noted, Swifties may not be happy with that one. "At the Knicks games, I would say it's very performative, because they just want to be seen at the game," Kolek said. "They're not necessarily fans." Both Kolek and Swift share Rhode Island connections. Kolek is from Cumberland and was a standout player at both Cumberland High and St. George's School. He played college ball at both George Mason and then Marquette, where he won Big East Player of the Year honors in 2022-23. He was drafted 34th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft by the Portland Trail Blazers but was traded to the New York Knicks on draft night. Swift, of course, is one of the most famous and successful singers on the planet. She is a 14-time Grammy Award winner and has compiled hundreds of other awards. In 2013, she bought a mansion in Watch Hill, formerly known as the “Holiday House," complete with an Olympic-sized swimming pool, a bedroom suite, and a past that ties it to the Standard Oil fortune. Swift married NFL star Travis Kelce on July 3 in a star-studded event at Madison Square Garden, after rumors swirled last year that the wedding could take place in Westerly. The Denver Nuggets have an interesting future, to say the least, especially when it comes to the core they have built over the last several seasons. This offseason, the team was unable to add significant pieces around superstars Jamal Murray and Nikola Jokic due to salary-cap restrictions. After this season, Jokic will have the opportunity to sign elsewhere rather than remain in Denver. Depending on how the year unfolds, teams are already preparing for the possibility that he could leave the Nuggets organization. “[Nikola Jokic] can profess his loyalty to the [Denver] Nuggets, there's still going to be teams that are positioning themselves and monitoring that. ... It's the same thing with Luka. He's done nothing but express optimism and excitement ... but it's not that long-term of an extension," ESPN’s Tim MacMahon said. The beginning of the season hasn't been particularly pleasant for Denver, as the team got off to a slow start. That included being booed by its own fans, something Jokic clearly wasn't happy about. “I think the fans that booed us are not welcome here anymore, if you ask me… if you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we came back from much worse for similar situations," Jokic said. The Nuggets are at a point where, if they don't perform well this season and believe Jokic could leave, they may have to seriously consider blowing up the roster. For that reason, NBA insider Zach Lowe has named Murray as a potential surprise trade candidate. “I said Jamal Murray just because if this team isn’t good, I think something is gonna crack here. I’m not closing the door,” Lowe said. A potential move involving Murray would certainly be a major development in Denver, especially considering the championship the organization won just a few years ago. However, the Nuggets have struggled to win playoff series since that title run. Murray is currently playing under a $207 million contract with the organization. He remains a valuable scorer and a veteran presence in the locker room. It also can't be overlooked that he has four years of team control remaining, meaning any team acquiring him would be adding a player who could remain part of its plans for years to come. item.title: Bengals' Burrow ahead of international debut: 'Means a lot' being here
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow speaks during a press conference ahead of the 2026 NFL Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons. (is associated with: «Bengals' Burrow ahead of international debut: 'Means a lot' being here») Nathalia Araújo/dpa Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said "it means a lot" to be in Madrid for his first-ever NFL game abroad as he aims to help the league expand the sport around the world. "It means a lot to me that I'm here. We're trying to build the game globally and I love being a part of that," Burrow said in a news conference on Friday. The quarterback has been very vocal in the past about his wish to play an international game and he will finally get the chance on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons at the Santiago Bernabéu. "I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people wake up. We're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch. We're gonna put on a show on Sunday," he said Burrow's career has been plagued by unfortunate injuries, while the Bengals missing the play-offs for the past three years. Ahead of the new season, the quarterback insisted he wanted to instil a sense of urgency in the locker room. Asked how satisfied he was with the urgency shown so far, Burrow said: "Very happy with the work that everybody is putting in, everyone want to be better. Nobody is content with where we're at right now. We're 5-2, but we have to be better than we were yesterday, than we were the day before." "We have guys that attack every day with that mentality. When you have people like that, that aren't satisfied, then you're just going to continue to get better and better throughout the season and that's what we've done." The Bengals are hoping to clinch their maiden win on international soil. In 2016, they played out a rare NFL draw, 27-27, against the Washington Commanders (back then Washington Redskins) in London. In their second trip to London in 2019, they were beaten 24-10 by the Los Angeles Rams. Coach Zac Taylor said he felt "really good" about the recent practice sessions in Spain and that he feels "our guys are in a good space right now" after getting acclimated to the time difference following a long trip. Despite the unusual attention from the international media, Taylor stressed that the team is trying to "make it as business as usual as possible." "You do want to embrace being over here and get to see some of the things the city has to offer. But when it's time to lock in on football, we lock in on football. It's been a pleasant experience for us. Lot more pleasant if we win the game on Sunday," the coach said.

item.title: ‘Back in a Non Toxic Environment,’ ‘Vibes Is High’ – Fans React to 76ers Teammates Hilariously Trolling LeBron James After Latest Milestone
item.description: ‘Back in a Non Toxic Environment,’ ‘Vibes Is High’ – Fans React to 76ers Teammates Hilariously Trolling LeBron James After Latest Milestone LeBron James became the first player in NBA history to make 16,000 regular-season field goals during the Philadelphia 76ers’ 112-106 win over the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday. His teammates teased him about it in the locker room afterward, and fans have been praising the chemistry around the veteran forward ever since. Some of those fans went further, holding James’ new surroundings up against his years with the Los Angeles Lakers, the team he played for last season. The win moved Philadelphia to 8-1, first in the Eastern Conference. Fans Praise 76ers Chemistry After Philadelphia Playres Tease LeBron James James’ 16,000th field goal came on a driving layup with 10:34 left in the second quarter, his second field goal of the night, and the NBA confirmed the milestone while the game was still going. He finished with 13 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists in 33 minutes. The ribbing came after the final buzzer, with the 76ers roster congratulating James by saying, “1-2-3, old as [expletive]. One fan wrote , “Glad he’s back in a non-toxic environment that actually appreciates him.” James first took the career record as a Laker, when he passed Kareem Abdul-Jabbar in Denver in March, months before he signed with Philadelphia. Another fan brought his old team into it, writing , “Lakers would have given the ball to someone else.” A third fan made the same comparison at greater length, writing that the Lakers “would’ve gotten that ball for a random bench player who scored 8 pts in that game instead of giving it to LeBron.” Other fans left Los Angeles out of it and focused on the group around James now, which includes Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. One asked , “When was the last time Bron has team vibes like this?” Another fan wrote , “At least they trolling and it’s out of love. Bron deserve that.” One user skipped the comparisons entirely and kept the focus on the room itself, writing that “the vibes is high in that locker room.” The Sixers visit the Lakers at Crypto.com Arena on December 25, a trip that will put the four-time champion back in the building he called home as a Laker, this time wearing No. 23 for Philadelphia. James’ 16,000th put him 163 makes ahead of Abdul-Jabbar’s career total of 15,837, and three more baskets Wednesday stretched the gap to 166. Abdul-Jabbar is the only other player in league history to reach even 14,000. Every basket the 41-year-old adds in a Sixers uniform widens that margin. item.description: The Atlanta Hawks brought CJ McCollum back on a one-year/$21 million contract this offseason . They also drafted Kingston Flemings with the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft. The idea was for the 35-year-old veteran guard to take the rookie under his wing. item.title: Detroit skyline, fictional Belle Isle golf hole to be featured by TGL
item.description: Motor City Golf Club won't play its matches in Detroit. But the city skyline still figures to play a prominent role in the upcoming seasons of TGL and WTGL. The indoor golf leagues recently unveiled new hole designs for TGL and WTGL, and among them is a 591-yard par 5 called "Belle of the Ball." The hole — which isn't real, but, man, it'd sure be cool if it was — tees off on Belle Isle, and finishes on an island green, with the Detroit skyline as the backdrop. The Belle Isle hole is one of 37 custom (and fictional) holes that will be used on a rotating basis in matches during the upcoming seasons of the simulator-golf leagues that were founded, in part, by Tiger Woods and Rory McIlory. WTGL starts its season this weekend, and TGL starts its season in December. Here is TGL's official description of the Belle Isle hole: Set on Belle Isle in the heart of the Detroit River, this par 5 begins with a signature landmark as the aiming point from the back tee and Canada stretching across the horizon in the distance. Bunkers split the center of the fairway, forcing players to choose their route from the start. The wider left side provides the safer target but leaves a long way home and makes reaching the (green) in two difficult. The narrow right side offers far less room for error, but a well-placed drive is rewarded with an opportunity to attack in two. After the tee shot, the hole turns back toward Detroit, bringing the downtown skyline into view and setting the stage for a dramatic approach into the Motor City. The inaugural WTGL season starts Sunday, Nov. 8, with Motor City Golf Club making its debut Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 8 p.m. against Los Angeles Golf Club. That match will be televised on ION. (Full schedule HERE .) The Motor City roster includes Brooks Koepka, Si Woo Kim, Jackson Koivun, Jake Knapp and Bud Cauley. The Motor City Golf Club franchises are owned by an investor group led by Michael Hamp and Peter Hamp, the sons of Detroit Lions owner Sheila Ford Hamp. Sheila Ford Hamp and husband, Steve, also are investors in the franchises, as is Denver Broncos owner Rob Walton.
